facts.text: The Credible Simulation Process is a German industry method for building credibility evidence into every step of a simulation project; ASAM QSQ is a standardization project seeking measurable simulation-quality metrics and was still unfinished in 2026.
facts.quote: The Credible Simulation Process is a German industry method for building credibility evidence into every step of a simulation project, and ASAM QSQ is a standardization project trying to define measurable simulation-quality metrics, still unfinished in 2026.

facts.text: The SET Level research consortium published the Credible Simulation Process in August 2021.
facts.quote: Published by the SET Level research consortium in August 2021

facts.text: Related work on the Credible Simulation Process includes the prostep ivip association's Simulation Credibility technical paper, version 8.1, dated 2024.
facts.quote: with related work by the prostep ivip association (Simulation Credibility technical paper, version 8.1, 2024)

facts.text: The Credible Simulation Process embeds credibility activities inside product development: defining the simulation task and its criticality, planning evidence, recording assumptions, verifying and validating throughout development, and carrying credibility information with models.
facts.quote: it embeds credibility activities inside product development: define the simulation task and its criticality, plan the evidence, record assumptions, verify and validate along the way, and carry credibility information with the models.

facts.text: M&S SPICE (2023) derives the credibility needed for a simulation task from the task's criticality and assesses whether the process can deliver that credibility.
facts.quote: A related method, M&S SPICE (2023), derives how much credibility a task needs from its criticality and assesses whether the process can deliver it

facts.text: ASAM is a standards association for automotive simulation data and interfaces.
facts.quote: ASAM is a standards association for automotive simulation data and interfaces.

facts.text: ASAM project P_2025_04, Quantifying Simulation Quality (QSQ), aims to standardize machine-readable simulation-quality metrics with use-case-specific weighting.
facts.quote: Its project P_2025_04, Quantifying Simulation Quality (QSQ), aims to standardize machine-readable simulation-quality metrics with use-case-specific weighting.

facts.text: ASAM states that no standardized metrics exist for assessing simulation quality, particularly sensor simulation.
facts.quote: ASAM itself states that "no standardized metrics exist" for assessing simulation quality, particularly sensor simulation

facts.text: The ASAM QSQ proposal workshop was held on 11 September 2025, and the project remained under way in 2026.
facts.quote: the proposal workshop was held on 11 September 2025 and the project was still under way in 2026

facts.text: The booklet classifies the Credible Simulation Process and ASAM QSQ as process templates from road-vehicle research, not proven off-road.
facts.quote: The booklet classifies both as process templates from road-vehicle research, not proven off-road

facts.text: The booklet concludes that simulation-credibility communities agree validation is required but have not agreed on metrics.
facts.quote: notes that the credibility communities agree validation is required but have not agreed on metrics

facts.text: The heavy off-road machine manufacturer can borrow simulation-credibility process discipline now, but must agree its own correlation metrics with its assessor rather than wait for a standard.
facts.quote: The manufacturer can borrow the process discipline now but must agree its own correlation metrics with its assessor rather than wait for a standard
